# Job Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 418r–418v

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Then Job answered and said:

**2** "Oh that my vexation were weighed,
and all my calamity laid in the balances!

**3** For then it would be heavier than the sand of the seas;
therefore my words have been rash.

**4** For the arrows of the Almighty are in me;
my spirit drinks their poison;
the terrors of God are arrayed against me.

**5** Does the wild donkey bray when it has grass,
or the ox low over its fodder?

**6** Can that which is tasteless be eaten without salt,
or is there any taste in the juice of the mallow?

**7** My appetite refuses to touch them;
they are as loathsome food to me.

**8** Oh that I might have my request,
and that God would grant my hope:

**9** that it would please God to crush me,
that he would let loose his hand and cut me off!

**10** This would still be my comfort;
I would exult in pain unsparing,
for I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

**11** What is my strength, that I should wait?
And what is my end, that I should be patient?

**12** Is my strength the strength of stones,
or is my flesh bronze?

**13** Have I any help in me,
when success has been driven from me?

**14** He who withholds kindness from a friend
forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

**15** My brothers are treacherous as a wadi,
as the channel of wadis that pass away,

**16** which are dark with ice,
and where the snow hides itself.

**17** When they grow warm they vanish;
when it is hot they are dried from their place.

**18** The caravans turn aside from their course;
they go up into the waste and perish.

**19** The caravans of Tema look,
the travelers of Sheba hope for them.

**20** They are ashamed because they trusted;
they come there and are confounded.

**21** For you have now become nothing;
you see terror and are afraid.

**22** Have I said, 'Make me a gift'?
Or, 'From your wealth offer a bribe for me'?

**23** Or, 'Deliver me from the enemy's hand'?
Or, 'Redeem me from the hand of the ruthless'?

**24** Teach me, and I will be silent;
make me understand how I have erred.

**25** How forceful are honest words!
But what does your reproof reprove?

**26** Do you think that you can reprove words,
when the speech of a despairing man is wind?

**27** You would even cast lots over the fatherless,
and bargain over your friend.

**28** But now, be pleased to look at me,
for I will surely not lie to your face.

**29** Turn now; let no injustice be done.
Turn now; my vindication is at stake.

**30** Is there any injustice on my tongue?
Cannot my palate discern what is ruinous?"

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Job 6 is Job's first direct response to Eliphaz, and it operates on two fronts: against God (vv.2-13) and against his friends (vv.14-30). Against God, Job is strikingly frank — God's arrows are in him, God's terrors are arrayed against him. He even wishes God would finish the job (v.9). Against his friends, the wadi metaphor (vv.15-20) is one of the most powerful images in the book — promising water in the dry season and delivering nothing. Job's challenge in verse 24 ("Teach me, and I will be silent") throws the burden of proof back on the friends. They claim he has sinned; let them prove it. This verse establishes the legal framework that will increasingly dominate Job's speeches — he wants a trial, not a sermon.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.6 — "juice of the mallow" vs. "white of an egg"
- **EMET:** "juice of purslane [chalamut]"
- **LOGOS:** "juice of the mallow"
- **PNEUMA:** "white of an egg"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "juice of the mallow" — Hebrew *chalamut* is botanically uncertain; "mallow" is the traditional identification. "White of an egg" follows the Talmudic interpretation but is less likely.

### V.14 — Syntax of kindness verse
- **EMET:** "To-the-despairing from-his-friend — kindness, or the-fear of-Shaddai he-forsakes"
- **LOGOS:** "He who withholds kindness from a friend forsakes the fear of the Almighty"
- **PNEUMA:** "A despairing person deserves loyalty from his friends, even if he has abandoned the fear of the Almighty"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Follows LOGOS — the verse means that withholding kindness from a suffering friend is itself a failure of piety. PNEUMA's reading reverses the conditional.

### V.21 — "become nothing" vs. "become nothing to me"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "you have now become nothing"
- **PNEUMA:** "That is what you have become to me — nothing"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "you have now become nothing" — the Hebrew *heyitem lo* (you have become "not") is stark and should remain unqualified.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
